**Finding: deviation (Section 17(b), paragraph p0118)**

- **Direction check:** The convenience right runs in our favour — Sparkling may terminate at will; Garman's only exits are insolvency events and uncured material default (17(c)), so there is no Vendor at-will right to strip out.
- **Gap 1 — notice:** 90 days is only our fallback; playbook preferred is 30 days.
- **Gap 2 — money:** 17(b) is silent on prepaid fees, even though refunds appear in the rejection (Section 8) and Garman-default (17(c)) paths, so we could fund unused licence/maintenance periods.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** 30 days' notice, express "for convenience, in whole or in part" language, no termination charge/penalty, and refund of prepaid fees within 30 days of the effective termination date. Fallback offered in the comment: 60 days' notice if the refund is retained.
